question: Unlike a normal friendship, what makes a professional nurse-patient relationship unique?

options.A: It lasts for the duration of a lifetime.
options.B: It focuses exclusively on social interaction.

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that nursing isn't just hanging out; every interaction has a clear purpose: helping your patient get better. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h1)

question: A nursing student only checks lab results and completely ignores how the patient is feeling. What important nursing concept is this student missing?
explanation: Spot on! Holistic care means treating the whole person—body, mind, and spirit—not just a disease on a lab sheet. Keep up the brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal when you build a therapeutic relationship with a patient?

options.A: Fulfilling the nurse's personal social needs

explanation: Exactly right! Everything we do as nurses is centered on helping the patient heal and feel better physically and emotionally. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient finally shares deep fears about their upcoming surgery after the nurse sits and listens quietly without rushing. What made this possible?

options.D: Documenting vital signs every fifteen minutes

explanation: Beautiful! When patients feel truly heard and safe with you, they open up. Active listening is your superpower as a nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h2)

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you and your patient first meet, set roles, and figure out what the problems are?
explanation: You got it! The orientation phase is all about breaking the ice, introducing yourself, and setting the stage for teamwork. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h3)

question: A patient is finally going home today after a smooth recovery. Which phase of the nurse-patient relationship are you in?
explanation: Well done! The termination phase marks a successful end to the relationship as the patient heads home. Such a rewarding moment! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which type of question is best for getting a patient to open up and share details about how they feel?
explanation: Awesome! Asking things like 'How are you feeling today?' invites a real story instead of a quick 'yes' or 'no'. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: A nurse crosses her arms and taps her foot while a patient is talking. How does this body language affect the chat?

options.A: It confirms the nurse is actively listening.
options.B: It creates a barrier to effective communication.
options.C: It demonstrates clinical authority to the patient.
options.D: It accelerates the patient interview process.

explanation: Spot on! Closed body language makes patients feel rushed or judged, so they close up. Keep your posture welcoming! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to building a good relationship with your patient?
explanation: You nailed it! Active listening builds bridges, not barriers. It's one of the best tools you have as a student nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: A busy nurse keeps cutting patients off mid-sentence because the ward is too packed. What is the likely result?

options.C: Impaired trust and withheld clinical information
options.D: Faster recovery times due to hospital efficiency

explanation: Correct! When we rush patients, they stop trusting us and might hide important symptoms we need to know. Take a deep breath—you'll learn to balance speed and care! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is it so important to maintain professional boundaries in nursing?

options.B: Preventing patients from asking personal questions
options.C: Protecting the safety and well-being of both patient and nurse
options.D: Ensuring the nurse receives adequate financial compensation

explanation: Brilliant! Boundaries keep both you and your patient safe, ensuring your care stays professional, objective, and helpful. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h6)

question: A nurse starts accepting expensive gifts from a patient and sharing heavy personal drama with them. What went wrong here?
explanation: You got it! Sharing too much personal life or taking costly gifts crosses the line from a professional helper to a personal buddy. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is a major danger when healthcare team members communicate poorly with each other?
explanation: Spot on! Clear communication between nurses, doctors, and pharmacists is literally a matter of patient safety. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h7)

question: A nurse uses the SBAR format to quickly update a doctor about a patient's crashing blood pressure. Why is SBAR so great?

options.A: It serves as a legal discharge document for the hospital.
options.B: It eliminates the physician's responsibility for treatment decisions.
options.C: It provides a structured, concise method for interprofessional communication.
options.D: It replaces the need for physical patient assessment.

explanation: Exactly right! SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) keeps things short, sweet, and organized when every second counts. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the first thing a nurse can do to fix personal communication biases?
explanation: You're doing amazing! Knowing your own biases helps you step back and give every single patient fair, equal care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why do clinical instructors encourage nursing students to write in a reflective journal?

options.A: It proves legal compliance with hospital shift hours.
options.B: It allows evaluation of past clinical interactions to improve future responses.
options.C: It replaces verbal handoff reports during shift changes.
options.D: It serves as the official medical chart for the patient.

explanation: Well done! Reflecting on your day helps you grow, celebrate your wins, and learn how to handle tricky moments even better next time. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h8)
